engagement.coverage_declaration: Only the advisory-matching finding is published.

findings.title: Tool callers choose the API host and proxy for requests that carry the server's Contentful management token
findings.evidence: exportSpace.ts declares transport-level knobs as ordinary tool inputs: line 99 `host: z.string().optional().describe('Management API host')`, line 100 `hostDelivery`, line 101 `proxy: z.string().optional().describe('HTTP/HTTPS proxy config')`, line 102 `rawProxy`. The handler then merges those caller values with the server's secret and hands the whole object to the network client: lines 134-140 `const exportOptions = { ...args, managementToken, ... } as any;` followed by line 148 `await contentfulExport.default(exportOptions)`. importSpace.ts is the same shape: `host` (line 69), `proxy` documented as accepting credentials `'HTTP/HTTPS proxy string (host:port or user:pass@host:port)'` (lines 70-73), `rawProxy` (lines 74-77), merged at lines 111-115 and passed at line 119. The `as any` cast on the merged object is what lets these fields reach the library untyped and unfiltered. The server already has an operator-controlled host — env.ts lines 9-13 `CONTENTFUL_HOST ... .default('api.contentful.com')`, plumbed through register.ts line 22 — and neither tool consults it or compares the argument against it.
findings.impact: The management token is the server's crown jewel: a Contentful CMA token with write access to every space the credential can reach. A single tool call with `host` or `proxy` set to an attacker-controlled endpoint sends that credential off-box. Because the caller is an LLM whose context is fed by content this very server reads, the injection path is short: hostile text in a CMS entry, asset description or webhook name instructs the agent to run the migration workflow with a custom host, and the operator sees a plausible 'export failed' message while the credential is already gone. Loss of the token is loss of the CMS: read, modify, publish and delete across the organisation, with no artefact left in the MCP transcript beyond one unusual argument.
findings.preconditions: The exportSpace/importSpace tools must be enabled, which per register.ts lines 81-95 requires a prior call to the spaceToSpaceMigrationHandler — an action available to the same caller. No operator interaction beyond approving the migration workflow itself is needed.
findings.recommendation: Remove `host`, `hostDelivery`, `proxy` and `rawProxy` from both input schemas. Build the options object from operator configuration first and spread caller arguments only over an explicit allowlist of content-selection fields, so that `{ ...args }` can never reintroduce a transport key: e.g. `const exportOptions = { ...pick(args, CONTENT_OPTION_KEYS), managementToken, host: config.host }`. If a non-default host is genuinely required for self-hosted or EU-region tenants, resolve it from CONTENTFUL_HOST in env.ts or from a static allowlist, never from tool input. Drop the `as any` casts so the compiler enforces the option surface.
findings.limits: The contentful-export and contentful-import packages were not read, so this file does not assert exactly which header carries the token to the custom host. The defect asserted is the one visible in scope: untrusted arguments controlling the destination of a request that the same code path authenticates with a server-held secret.
